findings.reason: diff.patch removes the guarded ẞ→ß replacement in src/common/utils.ts, and package.json has no `engines` field (grep found only ci.yml:23 `lts/*` and a node 24 workflow). On those runtimes the branch was unreachable and the [ẞ] fixture (test/fixtures/commonmark/good.txt:6673) still covers the path. Whether Node v10 is still supported isn't recorded anywhere, so the code can't settle whether this is a real regression.
findings.claim: Removing the Node v10 'ẞ'.toLowerCase() workaround from normalizeReference is not backed by a declared minimum runtime, so on Node v10 labels containing ẞ may stop matching ß/ss definitions.
findings.evidence: The diff removes from normalizeReference in src/common/utils.ts the guarded `if ('ẞ'.toLowerCase() === 'Ṿ') { str = str.replace(/ẞ/g, 'ß') }`, whose comment said 'remove this when node v10 is no longer supported'. package.json has no `engines` field, and CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:23) tests only `node-version: lts/*`, so nothing records or checks that Node v10 support has ended. On current runtimes the branch was unreachable, so behaviour there is unchanged, and the CommonMark fixture covering `[ẞ]` (test/fixtures/commonmark/good.txt:6673) still exercises the path.
